function: Hybrid DRL jointly designs BS transmit beamformers, RIS phase shifts and subcarrier assignment to minimise the squared position error bound (SPEB) under user SINR constraints; pp. 7-9.
system: Cooperative ISAC, two BSs with 4-antenna UPAs, passive reflecting RIS with P=20 to 40 elements, two single-antenna vehicular users, OFDMA; frequency band not stated; pp. 4, 12.
method: DDPG-based hybrid deep RL: actor-critic with continuous actions (beamformers, RIS phases) and discretised compound action (subcarriers); trained by reinforcement learning with replay buffer, 300 episodes; pp. 9-10, 12.
data_channel: Custom simulator: geometric channel model referenced as [52], i.i.d. CN(0, sigma^2) NLoS direct link, BS-to-BS sensing channel per [51]; no 3GPP or measured data; pp. 6, 12.
test_conditions: One simulated scenario (2 BSs, 2 users, 2 targets); P, noise, BS power, target position, L are varied; no stated test of a trained agent on unseen conditions; pp. 12-14.
baselines: Learned: ERPG (policy gradient) and IDD (integrated DDPG-DQN); non-learned: no RIS and random RIS phase shifts; pp. 12-13, Figs. 5-7.
metrics: SPEB (J) versus episodes, RIS elements, BS power, noise level and target position; running time per cycle versus BS antennas; beampattern gain; Figs. 4-10, pp. 12-14.
complexity: O(sum of layer-size products of actor and critic) (p. 12); running time per cycle roughly 190 to 230 s for 2 to 6 BS antennas (Fig. 9, p. 14).
q1_support: p. 12: "geometric channel model, referenced as [52]". The channel is a custom simulator (also i.i.d. CN(0, sigma^2) NLoS direct link, p. 6); no 3GPP TR 38.901/38.811, COST 2100, DeepMIMO or measured data is used.
q2_support: p. 12: "Fig. 4 plots J (SPEB) versus the number of episodes by varying P." Figs. 5-8 sweep P, power, noise and target position (Fig. 8 uses other BS and RIS positions, p. 14), but the paper never states that a trained agent is tested on conditions unseen in training or adapted to them.
q3_support: p. 13: "no RIS, random, and ERPG" (non-learned no RIS and random phases, Fig. 7). p. 12: "baseline schemes, such as ERPG and integrated DDPG-DQN (IDD)", plotted against HDRL on SPEB in Figs. 5-6 (p. 13).
q4_support: p. 12: "the total complexity of training and prediction is derived as" O(sum of actor and critic layer-size products). p. 14: "Fig. 9 displays how the running time, per cycle varies with the number of BS antennas".
q5_support: p. 12: "through numerical simulations". Channels are simulated; the paper gives no code or data link, no public dataset and no data-availability statement.
notes: Area 5 because the agent designs transmit beamformers, RIS phases and subcarriers that serve sensing (SPEB, objective 23a) and communication (SINR constraint 23d with served users, p. 7); the objective is a localization bound, so the reviewer should confirm this is ISAC design and not localization alone (excluded by function). ERPG and IDD are the authors' own implementations of standard DRL algorithms (p. 12), counted as standard learned baselines for q3. The reward is defined as minus SPEB at the terminal state (Eq. 24, p. 9), while p. 9 also says it is based on data rate and power usage. p. 10 states that HDRL is 'tested in simulated settings that mimic actual operational conditions', which is generic and reports no unseen-condition test, so q2 is 0. No frequency band is given (THz appears only in future work, p. 15).
